newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 22.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 22.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** The Cabinet Committe on Foreign Investment (CCFI) on Tuesday permitted Coca-Cola to retain a 100 percent stake in each of its two proposed bottling subsidiaries, the Business Standard reports.
The CCFI has however, asked the company to divest upto
49 percent of its stake within five years in any downstream bottling venture that these two subsidiaries set up, the paper says.
** The CCFI on Tuesday deferred discussion on the 24 billion rupee Tata-Singapore International Airline (Tata-SIA) venture, the Financial Express reports.
It says the discussion did not take place because Civil
Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim was unable to attend the CCFI meeting as he was not in New Delhi.
** The Indian cabinet approved a proposal to set up a $787 million power plant with 100 percent foreign equity in eastern India, a government statement said.
The cabinet approved foreign equity amounting to $236
million in the Kalinga Power Corporation Ltd which plans to set up a thermal power project in the state of Orissa, it said.
MARKETS:
** The Indian rupee opened steady at 35.85/86 against the dollar on Wednesday, dealers said. They expect the dollar to be stuck in the 35.84/87 range in the absence of major dollar demand.
A sell-off by speculators in major pivotals forced major
Indian bourses to end lower on Tuesday, dealers said.
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange.
ended 6.75 points, or 0.20 percent down, to 3,382.74 in range-bound trade.
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange eased 16.50 points to 960.50
** The Delhi index fell 1.38 points to 717.18
** The Madras index lost 13.82 points, to 3,253.58
** The Calcutta index dropped 1.0 to 437.51
